title: Plant vs Animal Cell
subject: Biology
summary: Fly in close to a plant cell and an animal cell and find out what makes them different.

missions.title: Two cells
missions.goalText: Meet the plant cell and the animal cell.
hints: One cell has a thick wall around it.
The plant cell is the box-shaped one.

missions.title: Cell wall
missions.goalText: Find what the cell wall is made of.
hints: The fibres are long strands that cross over each other.
Cellulose fibres make up the thick wall itself.

questions.prompt: What is the plant cell wall mainly made of?
questions.explanation: The plant cell wall is made mainly of cellulose. Its long fibres make the wall strong.

questions.prompt: Why does a plant cell keep a box-like shape?

options.label: Its nucleus holds it in shape
Its rigid cell wall supports it

questions.explanation: The rigid cell wall supports the plant cell and gives it a fixed, box-like shape.

missions.title: Cell membrane
missions.goalText: Find what controls what enters and leaves the cell.
hints: Proteins are the larger shapes sitting across the membrane.
Look for the shape with a passage through its middle.

questions.prompt: Why is the cell membrane called selectively permeable?

options.label: It lets some substances pass and stops others
It is found only in plant cells

questions.explanation: The cell membrane lets some substances pass and keeps others out, so it is selectively permeable.

questions.prompt: What is the cell membrane mainly made of?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is a double layer of lipids (phospholipids) with proteins set into it.

missions.title: Nucleus
missions.goalText: Find the parts of the nucleus.
hints: The nucleolus is the dark ball inside the nucleus.
Look through the open wedge of the envelope.

questions.prompt: Why is the nucleus called the control centre of the cell?

options.label: It holds the DNA that directs the cell's work

questions.explanation: The nucleus holds the DNA, the instructions that direct everything the cell does.

questions.prompt: What do nuclear pores do?

options.label: Let materials pass in and out of the nucleus

questions.explanation: Nuclear pores are openings in the envelope that let materials and messages pass in and out of the nucleus.

missions.title: Ribosomes
hints: The protein chain comes out of the large subunit.
It is the beaded strand leaving the top of the ribosome.

questions.prompt: What do ribosomes make?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes read the message from the nucleus and build proteins.

questions.prompt: Which part of the cell makes ribosomes?
questions.explanation: The nucleolus, inside the nucleus, makes ribosomes.

missions.title: Endoplasmic reticulum
missions.goalText: Tell rough ER from smooth ER.
hints: Smooth ER has no dots on it.
It looks like a tangle of smooth tubes.

questions.prompt: What makes rough ER look rough?
questions.explanation: Rough ER is studded with ribosomes, which make it look rough.

questions.prompt: Which job belongs to the smooth ER?
questions.explanation: Smooth ER makes lipids (fats) and helps remove harmful substances.

missions.title: Golgi apparatus
missions.goalText: Find out what the Golgi apparatus does.
hints: Think of a post office.
Vesicles carry its packages away.

questions.prompt: What are the small bubbles that bud off the Golgi apparatus called?
questions.explanation: Vesicles are small membrane bubbles that carry the packed materials away.

questions.prompt: Where do most proteins reach the Golgi apparatus from?
questions.explanation: Proteins made on the rough ER travel to the Golgi apparatus to be packed.

missions.title: Lysosomes
missions.goalText: Find what is inside a lysosome.
hints: The enzymes are the small particles inside.
Look inside the open bag.

questions.prompt: Why are lysosomes called suicide bags?

options.label: Their enzymes can digest the cell itself
They push water out of the cell

questions.explanation: If the cell is damaged, lysosomes can burst and their enzymes digest the cell itself.

questions.prompt: What keeps a lysosome's enzymes from digesting the rest of the cell?
questions.explanation: The lysosome's membrane keeps its digestive enzymes inside.

missions.title: Vacuoles
hints: It is the big, clear, pale blue sac.
Look in the plant cell.

questions.prompt: What fills a plant cell's central vacuole?
questions.explanation: The central vacuole is filled with cell sap: water with dissolved sugars and salts.

questions.prompt: How does a full vacuole help a plant?

options.label: It keeps the cell firm, so the plant stands upright

questions.explanation: A full vacuole presses against the cell wall and keeps the cell firm, so the plant stands upright.

missions.title: Mitochondria
missions.goalText: Find the parts of a mitochondrion.
hints: Look inside the opened mitochondrion.
The cristae are the shelves that fold in from the inner membrane.

questions.prompt: Which organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria release energy from food, so they are called the powerhouse of the cell.

questions.prompt: What are cristae?

options.label: Folds of the inner membrane of a mitochondrion
Stacks of discs inside a chloroplast
The outer covering of a cell

questions.explanation: Cristae are the folds of a mitochondrion's inner membrane. The fluid inside is the matrix.

missions.title: Chloroplasts
hints: Chloroplasts are green.
Look in the box-shaped plant cell.

questions.prompt: Which cells have chloroplasts?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are found in plant cells. Animal cells do not have them.

questions.prompt: In a chloroplast, what are the grana?
questions.explanation: The grana are stacks of thylakoids. The fluid around them is the stroma.

missions.title: Recap
hints: Chloroplasts are only in plant cells.

questions.prompt: A cell has mitochondria, but no cell wall and no chloroplasts. Which kind of cell is it?

options.label: A cell from a green leaf

questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cell wall, and green plant cells have chloroplasts. A cell with neither is an animal cell.

questions.prompt: Why do plant cells need chloroplasts?

options.label: To give the cell its shape

questions.explanation: Chloroplasts use sunlight to make food. Mitochondria release energy from that food.
